source: Cambodian rice cultivation training slide deck (Khmer language, PowerPoint-derived; publisher/presenter and exact date not stated on the visible slides; slide 19 of a 21-slide deck on rice crop ecosystems, morphology, growth stages, fertilizer use, and cultivation practice; cites CARDI (Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute); uploaded file 26af386d-5c09dd22672cefcf11fb5b6d671175801533697315.pdf)
text:
Fertilizer schedule for transplanted rice, following CARDI (Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute) recommendations:

Basal application (applied at/before transplanting): organic fertilizer (compost/manure) at 3-5 tonnes per hectare per CARDI guidance; plus chemical fertilizer 15-15-15 at 100 kg per hectare and DAP at 25 kg per hectare.

Top-dressing applications: 1st top-dressing applies Urea at 50 kg per hectare, representing approximately 40% of the total urea to be applied over the season; 2nd top-dressing applies Urea at 40 kg per hectare, representing approximately 30% of the total.

Note: this schedule (basal organic 3-5 t/ha, 15-15-15 at 100 kg/ha, DAP 25 kg/ha, two urea top-dressings of 50 kg/ha then 40 kg/ha) applies to transplanted rice per this slide, and differs in its rate structure from the broadcast/direct-seeded fertilizer schedule shown elsewhere in the same deck (15-15-15 or DAP 18-46-00 basal, with two flat 46-00-00 urea top-dressings at 15 and 30 days after sowing) — the two schedules are for different establishment methods (transplanted vs. direct-seeded/broadcast) and are not necessarily in conflict, but are flagged here so they are not confused with one another.
